title: Brass players need rest, and Mingus punching a trombonist
summary: He says Mingus did not grasp that brass players must breathe, and Mingus's anger at trombonist led to injury.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: I used to do some of the same things. I would have the trumpets and the trombones playing as much as I did the saxophones. And it took me a long time to realize that, hey, a cupped instrument cannot be played as long as a saxophone. These guys have to rest. The brass instruments have to rest. And that's something that they... He probably found it out near the end, but he didn't know that then. So during his earlier writings, everything was almost impossible to play, because he didn't think of the difficulty of a wind instrument. Like, a string player can play forever, you know; they don't have to breathe. But when you play a brass instrument, you must breathe and have time to rest and get some blood back in your chops. So that's one of the things that he had to learn.
He never took up the tuba, right?

No, he didn't fool with the tuba. Bass was his thing, and he played a little piano, too. So consequently, he was not hip to brass instruments having to breathe. He'd get angry, and he might punch a trombone player in the mouth...
Which he did, you know, which is ridiculous. Because when your teeth and your lips are sore, you cannot
play a brass instrument. You might get a long with a saxophone, because that's a different approach.
And the trombone player that he hit couldn't play for a year or so.
Well, there you go. Do you want to leave Mingus now and go somewhere else?
